title: Entropy-aware Canary Strategy Compiler
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a compiler component that translates high-level canary strategies into executable step schedules, traffic splits, and automated guardrails. The compiler should produce conservative default schedules but allow entropy-aware adaptations based on live signals (drift, output diversity, and metric variance).
background: Current rollout tooling accepts static step schedules and separate guardrail rules. Operators frequently over- or under-shift traffic because the schedule doesn't account for signal volatility or non-stationary traffic patterns. As models and workloads get more diverse, fixed increments cause either slow rollouts or unnecessary rollbacks. We need a middle layer that reasons about uncertainty and produces safer, workload-aware rollouts.
proposed_solution: Create a new 'Strategy Compiler' service that ingests a developer-facing policy (strategy DSL) and emits: 1) an execution plan (time-boxed steps with target traffic fractions), 2) adaptive wait windows (variable duration per step based on signal confidence), 3) dynamic step sizes (entropy-aware increments), and 4) a concrete set of guardrail checks wired to the Console alerting and rollback circuits. The compiler will include a Bayesian change-point detector to lengthen wait times when signals are noisy and shorten when signals are stable. It will also provide a 'shadow surface' tuning parameter to mirror X% of traffic for offline evaluation during rollout. Default behavior: start conservative (1% -> 5% -> 15% -> 40% -> 100%) but modify steps +/- based on measured entropy metric.
config_schema:
Example strategy DSL (string):
name: entropy-canary
base_schedule: [1,5,15,40,100]
max_step_increase: 2.0  # multiplier when low-entropy
min_step_increase: 0.5  # multiplier when high-entropy
entropy_metric: output_entropy
entropy_thresholds: {low: 0.2, high: 0.6}
adaptive_wait: true
wait_bounds_minutes: {min: 10, max: 120}
shadow_fraction: 0.05
rollback_cooldown_minutes: 30
guardrails:
  - name: latency_p95_pct_increase
    window: 5m
    threshold: 1.25
    action: rollback
  - name: error_rate_absolute
    window: 5m
    threshold: 0.01
    action: pause
This config is compiled into an ordered plan that the rollout executor understands.
rollout_plan: Execution plan generated by compiler should include: 1) compiled_steps: list of {percent, expected_duration_minutes, reason}, 2) observability hooks: metric set and cadence, 3) shadow wiring: if shadow_fraction > 0, configure mirroring route, 4) rollback circuits: cooldown windows and immediate rollback triggers. Example flow: compile -> dry-run simulation (historical replay) -> submit to rollout executor with metadata -> monitor and adapt. Dry-run must simulate at least the last 7 days of traffic to estimate entropy and expected variance.
guardrails: Guardrail catalog the compiler can synthesize: - Relative latency uplift (P95) over baseline with multiplier thresholds - Absolute error rate increases - Regression on quality signals (semantic similarity, BLEU-like or eval model score) - Token-level cost spikes - Drift in input distribution (KL divergence) with thresholds - Shadow vs live output divergence. Each guardrail must map to one of three actions: pause, rollback, or alert-and-keep-watching. Actions should include a human-notify path when confidence is low.
metrics: Primary signals used by compiler: 'latency_p95', 'error_rate', 'model_eval_score_delta', 'output_entropy', 'input_kl_divergence', 'tokens_per_request', 'cached_hit_rate'. We will expose a composite 'rollout_confidence' score in the Console derived from variance-normalized z-scores; it drives adaptive_wait and step adjustments.
risks: 1) Overfitting compiler heuristics to a narrow set of workloads -> mitigate by training heuristics on multi-tenant historical data and including a conservative safety floor. 2) Latency of decision loop (too slow to rollback) -> mitigate by keeping immediate rollback triggers outside the adaptive loop and wired directly to executor. 3) Complexity for users -> mitigate by sensible defaults and a Console guided editor with 'simple' vs 'advanced' modes.
infra_dependencies: requires: rollout-executor API (ENG-45711), metrics ingestion and retention changes (ENG-51642), and a simulation runner with historical traffic access (infra team). Also needs Console UI hooks for showing entropy and confidence.
